findings.rule: Smell baseline — Duplicated Code (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3)
findings.title: The RestateWorkPanel mount block is duplicated verbatim (in shape) in two files
findings.evidence: work-question-panel.tsx:179-186 mounts `<RestateWorkPanel work={{ id: data.record.work_id, basis: data.record.basis ?? null }} clientId={data.record.client_id} session={sessionTokenAccessor} onRestated={reload} />`; apps/web/components/parts/WorkCards.tsx's `WorkQuestionCard` (around line 332) mounts the identical shape: `<RestateWorkPanel work={{ id: data.record.work_id, basis: data.record.basis ?? null }} clientId={part.client_id} session={sessionTokenAccessor} onRestated={reload} />`. Both exist because WorkQuestionCard bypasses WorkQuestionPanel and mounts WorkQuestionForm directly, so `offerRestate` cannot reach it — but the fix duplicates the mounting shape rather than sharing it.
findings.required_fix: Extract a small shared helper (e.g. a `<RestateForQuestionRecord record clientId onRestated/>` wrapper, or a hook returning the props) that both call sites use, so a future change to how a WorkQuestionRecord maps onto RestateWorkPanel's props cannot drift between the two copies. Judgement call, not a hard violation — two call sites of a four-line JSX shape is a small duplication.

findings.rule: .claude/skills/tdd/SKILL.md — "One slice at a time" / "Red before green"; WORK-ORDER.md rule 4
findings.title: Two of the four terms of clara._source_corrected_work's rule were implemented before a dedicated red test existed for them
findings.evidence: Commit 63358cd19 ("feat(db): #885 a document-fact correction cancels and re-admits...") lands the COMPLETE four-term rule in `clara._source_corrected_work` — pending question, cites this document, NO committed receipt (term c), and restatable status (term d) — backed by only 2 test cells (w885.supersede.cancels, w885.answer.superseded), neither of which exercises terms (c) or (d). The two carve-out cells that actually exercise (c) and (d) — w885.posted.untouched and w885.terminal_residue.ignored — are added only in the following commit, 48c9e6387 ("test(db): #885 the three carve-outs..."), with no accompanying SQL change. So the SQL for those two carve-outs existed before a red test drove it, which is implementation-ahead-of-test at the level of two of the rule's four conjuncts, inside an otherwise correctly-sliced ticket.
findings.required_fix: None required retroactively — both terms are now covered (verified green: 6/6 in work-source-correction-supersede.test.mjs, re-run on the rig). Flagging as a process note for future migrations of this shape: land each conjunct of a multi-term predicate behind its own red test before writing it, or say explicitly in the commit message that the whole predicate was modelled on an already-proven precedent (clara.list_source_dependents' work_questions arm) and reviewed rather than test-driven per term. This is a judgement call, not a hard violation — the commit message does claim a vacuity check per new cell ("each proven non-vacuous by deliberately breaking the one rule and watching it go red"), and all six cells reproduce green on re-run.

findings.rule: WORK-ORDER.md rule 2 ("One ticket = its own commits, whose messages name it... every commit message ends with Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
findings.title: One commit in the lane's history departs from the lane's own commit-message convention
findings.evidence: Commit 9df3f0df5, "fix(web): unblock the build — SelectValue's kind roster used the wrong constant", carries no ticket number in its subject line (the commit body says "Pre-existing bug, unrelated to #905") and ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` plus a `Claude-Session:` trailer, not the lane's `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>` every other commit in this lane carries. The fix itself is correct, one line, and necessary (it unblocked `next build`'s TypeScript pass, which was blocking every e2e walk in the worktree including #905's own gate), so this is a process/attribution note rather than a code-quality issue.
findings.required_fix: None functionally required. For future lane hygiene: a cross-cutting, non-ticket build-unblock commit should still carry the lane's own commit-message and attribution convention, or be called out explicitly as an out-of-band fix in the ticket report (it is: 905's own report should say so).

positive_notes: All four migrations (0265-0268) follow the house shape precisely: statement_timeout/lock_timeout set first, prestate pins measured on the live rig (re-measured independently and confirmed matching), body, tail census re-reading the committed catalog, owner/SECURITY DEFINER-or-INVOKER/search_path/ACL all explicitly re-asserted and verified unchanged where claimed.

0268's lock-order argument (Work rungs before clara.documents, to avoid an ABBA against clara._lock_document_binding) is asserted positionally in the tail (position() comparisons) and independently reproduces green.

The #957 redo of 0268 (commit 4dc9acac4, comment-only) is exactly the documented exception in WORK-ORDER.md's migrations rule (own unmerged migration, highest applied version, recorded as done) — not a violation of 'never edit an applied migration'.

TDD vertical-slicing is otherwise well observed: each db feat commit pairs its migration with its own test file in the same commit, each web feat commit is its own ticket-scoped commit, and the new work-question-panel.tsx logic was deliberately extracted into a pure, exported `offersRestateFor` function specifically so a test could reach it without mocking the Supabase session seam.

Shared files (CONTEXT.md, en.json, apps/web/test/manifest.txt, packages/db/tests/rig-meta.mjs, packages/db/package.json) were all touched minimally and at sorted/logical positions, consistent with the multi-lane shared-file rule.

The in-file migration-frontier skip helpers added to work-list.test.mjs and client-work-pack.test.mjs (gateClaimLabel/gateReceiptWindow) are a reasonable, precedented substitute for a global preintegration-gate.mjs module when the ticket only widens an EXISTING shared test file rather than adding a new one.
summary: Standards axis: no hard violations of a documented repo standard were found in the SQL or TypeScript logic itself — all four migrations reproduce their prestate/tail claims live on the rig and every re-run test file is green. The one repeated, citable rule violation is documentation: three of the four tickets' migrations (0265/#839, 0266/#880, 0267/#905) are missing the packages/db/README.md section that WORK-ORDER.md rule 9 requires and that this README's own convention gives every other migration through the base commit. One small Duplicated Code smell (a four-line RestateWorkPanel mount repeated in two files) and one TDD process note (two carve-out terms implemented before their own red test, though later covered and verified) are judgement calls, not blockers. One commit departs from the lane's commit-message/attribution convention but is otherwise a correct, necessary, disclosed fix.
